proof.text: The finite-presentation hypothesis includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Its affine presentations $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ are generated by the images of the finitely many variables over $R$, so $f$ is locally of finite type and hence of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to $f$ and the integral base $S$. It gives a nonempty open $U_0\subseteq S$ on which $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Choose a nonempty affine open $U\subseteq U_0$. It is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and contains the generic point of $S$; restricting the affine charts preserves the two properties. No Noetherian or separatedness hypothesis on $X$ is used.

source.place: Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness, structure-sheaf case; choose an affine subopen of the generic-flat open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] with $T=S$, $W=X$ and this $U$. The base is qcqs by hypothesis, $U$ is quasi-compact, $f$ is finite type and quasi-separated, and its restriction over $U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by Step 1. Obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, its blowup $b:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}S\to S$, and the strict transform $X_1\subseteq Y:=X\times_SS_1$. The theorem says exactly that $X_1\to S_1$ is flat and of finite presentation. Let $V=S\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, so $U\subseteq V$ and $\eta\in V$.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, statement and construction of the strict transform.

proof.text: The finite-type ideal $\mathcal I$ makes $b$ proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper]. On a finite affine cover of $S$, finite generation of $\mathcal I$ expresses $V$ as a finite union of principal affine opens, hence $V$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $b$ is $V$-admissible because $\mathcal I|_V=\mathcal O_V$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Thus [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] gives the specified isomorphism $b^{-1}(V)\simeq V$ over $V$. In particular the actual base change $S_1\times_S\eta\to\eta$ is an isomorphism, so its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

source.place: Tags 02NS/02OS, properness for a finite-type ideal and the isomorphism away from the centre.

proof.text: The global blowup is obtained by gluing the affine local blowups over an affine cover of $S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data, def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model]. The open embeddings and covering of this glued scheme are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]; the overlap opens are the inverse images of the base overlaps in the cited datum. On a nonempty member $\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A$ is a domain and $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Write $I=\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}A)=(a_0,\ldots,a_r)$. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] its blowup is covered by $\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/a_i])$. A zero $a_i$ gives the empty chart; for $a_i\ne0$, the definition [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] places $A[I/a_i]$ between $A$ and $K$, so it is a domain with fraction field $K$. Every nonempty chart therefore has the same dense generic point, namely the point of $b^{-1}(\eta)$ identified in Step 3. Hence $S_1$ is reduced and irreducible and is nonempty; it is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Finally a proper morphism has closed image [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The image of $b$ contains $V$, a nonempty open of the integral $S$, so is all of $S$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; domain calculation on blowup charts and closed-image argument. Schemes Tags 01JB/01JC give the gluing cover; Divisors Tag 02ND gives the same integral-blowup conclusion.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], $X_1$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of the open $Y_V:=Y\times_SV$ in $Y$, with closed inclusion $a:X_1\hookrightarrow Y$. This inclusion is finite: on every affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $B/J$ is generated as a $B$-module by $1$; apply the affine definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The inclusion $Y_V\to Y$ is quasi-compact: on any affine chart the pulled-back finite-type ideal has finitely many generators, and the complement of its zero set is a finite union of principal opens. It is quasi-separated since its diagonal is an isomorphism. Thus [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] applies to this open inclusion and the target open $Y_V$. The restricted scheme image is the image of $\operatorname{id}_{Y_V}$, which is $Y_V$ itself because its restriction kernel is zero. Consequently $a^{-1}(Y_V)\to Y_V$ is an isomorphism. Put $U_1=Y_V$. Since $\eta\in V$, the actual induced generic-fibre map $a_\eta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; Morphisms Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, restriction to an open.

proof.text: The generic fibre is schematically dense in the flat $S_1$-scheme $X_1$. Indeed, over a nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S_1$ and an affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X_1$ mapping into it, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ a flat $A$-module. Here $A$ is a domain with fraction field $K$ [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Tensor the injection $A\hookrightarrow K$ with $B$; flatness in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] gives $B\hookrightarrow B\otimes_AK$. The ring $B\otimes_AK$ is the ring of the actual generic-fibre chart by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Thus a section on this affine chart which vanishes on the generic fibre is zero. Applying this to an affine cover of any open of $X_1$ proves that all its sections are determined by their generic-fibre restrictions.

source.place: Generic-density calculation after Tag 081R: flatness tensors the domain-to-fraction-field injection to an injection.

proof.text: The open $a^{-1}(U_1)$ contains the whole generic fibre of $X_1$. A section on any open of $X_1$ which restricts to zero on its intersection with $a^{-1}(U_1)$ therefore restricts to zero on the generic fibre, and is zero by Step 6. This is exactly injectivity of $\mathcal O_{X_1}\to j_*\mathcal O_{a^{-1}(U_1)}$ [def-trf-schematically-dense-open]. Hence the inverse-image inclusion is schematically dense, as asserted in the corrected statement. The construction makes no density assertion for $U_1\subseteq Y$: flatness was established for the strict transform, and vertical components of $Y$ can be absent from it.

source.place: Tag 080D, strict-transform source; schematic-density verification using the injection of Step 6.

title: Finite generic flatification after a birational base modification
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where quasi-compact quasi-separated means that it has a finite affine open cover with quasi-compact pairwise intersections. Let $f:X\to S$ be dominant and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; dominant means that its image is dense. Write $K=k(S)=\mathcal O_{S,\eta}$ for its function field [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$ for its generic point [def-sc-generic-point]. There exist an integral scheme $S_1$, a proper surjective morphism $b:S_1\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, and a finite morphism $a:X_1\to X\times_S S_1$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] such that $a_\eta$ is an isomorphism, there is an open $U_1\subset X\times_S S_1$ over which $a$ is an isomorphism and whose inverse-image inclusion in $X_1$ is schematically dense [def-trf-schematically-dense-open], and $X_1\to S_1$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The generic fibre is schematically dense in $X_1$, meaning that sections of $\mathcal O_{X_1}$ on any open are determined by their restrictions to its generic fibre. No schematic density of $U_1$ in the possibly nonflat target $X\times_S S_1$ is asserted.
